status_note: Covered by [apache/datafusion#26138](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/26138) (open, the epic for `-0.0` and NaN keys) and the open PR #26091 (`-NaN = NaN`). The zero sign is fixed by 55.0.0 (`-0.0 = 0.0` is TRUE and they group together); NaN signs and payloads still count as different values.
summary: Doubles compare by `f64::total_cmp`: on 51.0.0 `-0.0 < 0.0` and the two zeros are two groups; on 51.0.0 and 55.0.0 a NaN and a negative NaN (or two NaN payloads) are different values in `DISTINCT`, grouping and joins. The reference has one zero and one NaN (D10).
repro: `select k, count(*) from (values (0.0), (-0.0)) t(k) group by k` gives two groups on 51.0.0, one on 55.0.0.
`select count(distinct v) from (values (cast('NaN' as double)), (-cast('NaN' as double))) t(v)` gives `2` on both.
handling: DataFusion is a tier-3 engine. Tables handed to it and its results are canonicalised (`sverify.engine.canonical`); `--write-datafusion` refuses plans whose double operations can make `-0.0` or a negative NaN (#1165), and the DataFusion tests of computed doubles skip citing this entry.
found_by: audit of DataFusion's limits on the shared path (2026-11-08)
